title: Chapter 3 Quiz: The Shared Responsibility Model
description: Test your understanding of who secures what in the cloud.

questions.question: The phrase 'security OF the cloud' refers to:
options: The provider's physical and infrastructure security
questions.explanation: 'Of the cloud' is the provider's responsibility – physical hardware, network, and facilities.

questions.question: The customer is responsible for security _____ the cloud.
questions.explanation: You secure what you put 'in' the cloud – data, apps, access.

questions.question: In the shared responsibility model, the cloud provider is always responsible for patching the guest operating system.
questions.explanation: Only in managed (PaaS) or serverless services does the provider patch the OS. In IaaS, it's the customer's job.

questions.question: For an Amazon EC2 instance, which of the following is the customer's responsibility?
options: Physical security of the data centre
Applying security patches to the Windows OS
questions.explanation: The customer manages the guest OS, including its patches.

questions.question: Who is responsible for configuring an S3 bucket policy that prevents public access?
options: Neither – S3 buckets are always private
questions.explanation: AWS provides the tools; the customer must configure them correctly.

questions.question: AWS is responsible for encrypting data at rest in S3 by default, with no action needed from the customer.
questions.explanation: While AWS now encrypts new objects by default using SSE-S3, the customer must still ensure the setting is applied and, for compliance, may need to manage their own keys.

questions.question: Azure's shared responsibility model uses which terminology?
options: Security of the cloud / Security in the cloud
Security of the platform / Security on the platform
questions.explanation: Azure calls it 'of the platform' (Microsoft) and 'on the platform' (customer).

questions.question: In Google Cloud, who is responsible for patching the worker nodes in a GKE Standard cluster?
options: Google patches the control plane, customer patches worker nodes
questions.explanation: In Standard mode, you manage the worker nodes, including OS updates.

questions.question: With AWS Lambda, the customer is responsible for securing the underlying runtime environment.
questions.explanation: AWS manages the runtime and execution environment. The customer is responsible for the function code and IAM role.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon RDS for a critical database. Who is responsible for taking regular backups and testing restore procedures?
options: The customer must configure and verify backups
Backups are not needed for RDS
questions.explanation: RDS can perform automated backups, but you must enable them, set retention, and test restores.

questions.question: In the apartment analogy, the landlord maintaining the building's fire alarm is like the provider's responsibility for security ______ the cloud.
questions.explanation: The building's fire alarm is part of the infrastructure (of the cloud), like the provider's physical security.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common misunderstanding of the shared responsibility model?
options: The customer is responsible for data encryption
The provider will back up all data automatically
Physical security is the provider's job
questions.explanation: Many customers wrongly assume backups are automatic and fully managed by the provider.

questions.question: On Google Cloud, using customer‑managed encryption keys (CMEK) transfers all encryption responsibility to Google.
questions.explanation: You still manage key access and rotation; Google only performs the encryption operation using your keys.

questions.question: For an Azure App Service (PaaS) web application, the customer is responsible for:
questions.explanation: Azure manages the OS and runtime; the customer must secure the app code and any third‑party libraries.

questions.question: If a developer leaves an API key hardcoded in a Lambda function, whose responsibility is the resulting exposure?
questions.explanation: Secure coding practices are always the customer's domain, regardless of the service model.

questions.question: Using AWS Config rules can help monitor whether your resources comply with your shared responsibility obligations.
questions.explanation: AWS Config can check for misconfigurations like open S3 buckets, helping you uphold your side of the model.

questions.question: Which term describes the practice of documenting responsibility per service?
questions.explanation: A responsibility matrix explicitly maps each security task to the provider or customer.

questions.question: In the shared responsibility model, identity and access management (IAM) is:
questions.explanation: Controlling who can access your cloud resources is fundamentally your job.

questions.question: GCP's default encryption at rest means the customer has no responsibility regarding encryption.
questions.explanation: You still need to manage access to the data and may need to manage keys or verify encryption settings for compliance.

questions.question: AWS secures the hypervisor; you secure the _______ operating system on your EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: The guest OS is the operating system running inside your virtual machine – your responsibility.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to avoid gaps in the shared responsibility model?
options: Read the service‑specific shared responsibility documentation for every service used
questions.explanation: Each service has a different boundary; the official documentation is the only reliable source.
